predictions: P-A (integrated Ep, the one real cross-frame test): the fresh blind integrated fit over the stamped window 75.629-108.915 s - which includes ~6.5 s more decaying tail than the archival 76.795-102.369 s and matches the catalog fluence interval 76.80-108.54 s to within ~1.2 s - will land Band Ep BELOW the archival 245.7 (-16.1/+16.7) keV and within ~1.5 sigma of the catalog 208.7 +- 15.3 keV, i.e. PREDICTED Ep in 195-235 keV, with alpha in [-0.78,-0.62] and beta in [-2.55,-2.05]. FALSIFIER: an integrated Ep > 250 keV or < 180 keV, or alpha outside [-0.90,-0.55]. If Ep stays near 246 keV while covering the catalog's own interval, the 37 keV offset is NOT tail coverage - and since the detector set is IDENTICAL (n7,n8,nb,b1), the residual cause would have to be response handling, background model, or statistic, which the P3 diff must then name.

P-B (BB / union rule): predict union count = 0 AGAIN - no block reaching LRT_BANDBB_BAND >= 9.2 or LRT_CPLBB_CPL >= 9.2 with kT > 1.05 (archival maxima 7.018 and 4.668, both in the integrated row). Predict AIC nevertheless keeps naming a +BB model in the integrated row and in the pulse core, at margins < 5. FALSIFIER: any block passing the union rule under the L18+ engine -> the archival zero was a seed/cap artifact (L8/L9 class), bn101225377 joins the BB population, and kT is expected in 7.5-11 keV (archival kT: Band+BB 7.81/10.97/7.49/7.62; CPL+BB 8.28/10.79/8.17/7.60). Either outcome is a publishable data point because NO paper has ever tested a thermal component in this burst - there is no literature claim to agree or disagree with.

P-C (break structure / the two-break question): predict NO valid two-break block. Archival LRT_DSBPL_SBPL maxes at 5.639 (integrated) with DSBPL_VALID=False in every real block, and the catalog's own SBPL fit (E_break = 128.04 +- 13.74 keV, indices -0.894/-2.216) is a single-break description of the same data. FALSIFIER: a DSBPL_VALID block with dAIC >= 10 over SBPL in the fresh run.

P-D (model indifference - the characteristic feature of this burst): predict the fresh run reproduces near-degeneracy, best-minus-second AIC margin < 5 in EVERY block (archival margins 0.10, 0.24, 2.01, 2.52 - all far below the project's dAIC >= 10 doctrine). FALSIFIER: a decisive winner (dAIC >= 10) anywhere; that would signal an engine change, not new information in the data.

P-E (binning coverage): predict the fresh 27b binning of 75.629-108.915 s extends past 104 s (the archival binning stopped at 102.369 s while counts persist to ~108 s) and yields 3-5 blocks, with the last block the softest and least constrained. FALSIFIER: a fresh binning that again stops before 103 s.

P-F (bound-capping diagnosis, L9/L19): predict the L18+ engine labels the archival railings explicitly - blk2 Band beta = -5.000 (zero negative error, BAND_VALID=False) and SBPL beta = -4.999 in blk0/blk2 - as BOUND_CAPPED rather than propagating them as silent invalidity, and that widened caps move blk2's Band beta off the rail (predicted beta < -2.5 but not at the bound).

P-G (spectral evolution): predict hard-to-soft across the first two blocks - Ep(blk0) > Ep(blk1) at >1 sigma (archival 411.8 -96.9/+146.3 vs 226.8 -13.6/+15.4) - and predict the tail block remains UNCONSTRAINED (Ep error > 50% ) rather than showing a real re-hardening, despite the archival blk2 central value of 279 keV. FALSIFIER: a tail-block Ep constrained to better than 25% and higher than the pulse-core Ep, which would be a genuine re-hardening worth a paragraph.
